title: FCI Leavenworth Cable Television Services
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Institution Leavenworth, requests quotations for cable television services from eligible vendors. Quotation Requirements: Vendors shall submit: � A proposed channel lineup identifying how it meets the SOW requirements and clearly identifying any substitutions or exceptions. � A brief technical approach explaining how service will be provided to approximately 115 television drops at the FCI and FPC using the existing distribution system. Identify any equipment, installation, or modifications required and describe responsibility for equipment maintenance and repairs. � A transition approach identifying the time required to activate service and measures to minimize service interruptions. � A description of telephone support, outage assessment, on-site response, and service restoration capabilities. � References for up to three recent, relevant contracts involving comparable television distribution services. Vendors without relevant past performance shall state that in their quotation. � Separate pricing for the base period and each of the four option periods, including recurring service, installation, equipment, preventive maintenance, and any other charges necessary to perform the SOW. Identify any exceptions to the requested terms. Comparative Evaluation: The Government will use a comparative evaluation to determine which quotation provides the best value. Quotations will be compared directly against one another using technical capability, past performance, and price. Numerical scores will not be assigned. Technical capability will consider the proposed channel lineup, compatibility with the existing distribution system, installation and transition approach, and ability to meet maintenance and outage-response requirements. Past performance will consider available information regarding successful performance of similar services, including reliability, responsiveness, and customer satisfaction. A vendor without relevant past performance will receive a neutral assessment under this factor. Technical capability and past performance, when combined, are more important than price. The Government may select a higher-priced quotation when its documented benefits justify the additional price. Total evaluated price will include the base period, all four option periods, and all required charges. Evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise them. Select Best-Suited, Then Negotiate: The Government intends to select the best-suited vendor based on the initial quotations but reserves the right to conduct exchanges. After identifying the apparent best-suited vendor, the Government may negotiate price, technical details, transition arrangements, or other terms with that vendor to finalize the requirement and obtain the best value. Identification as the apparent best-suited vendor does not constitute an award. If the parties cannot reach an acceptable agreement, the Government may end negotiations and engage the next best-suited vendor based on the evaluation. Vendors should submit their best initial quotations because the Government may make award without exchanges. Quotations must include: legal business name, business address, UEI, a point of contact, telelphone number, and e-mail address. All quotations must be submitted by e-mail to FCI Leavenworth Contract Specialist Kathleen Wood at kwood1@bop.gov.

title: Weapons Effect Solicitation
description: This solicitation is related to Notice IDs: N00167-25-RFP-CD-66-0014 and N00167-25-RFP-CD-66-0014_Rev1. The contractor shall provide scientific and technical services with experts in UNDEX and AIREX analysis of undersea and surface vessels to develop and utilize specialized software codes that: 1) Aid in the selection of live fire events and provide support to live fire test and evaluation programs; 2) Simulate an underwater shock environment from a far field or near miss location; 3) Simulate the response of Navy platforms to UNDEX and AIREX for far field, near miss, contact, and internally detonating weapon attacks; 4) Check the integrity of computational models; 5) Solve finite element models elastic-plastic response and reduced order engineering tools to UNDEX and AIREX events; and 6) Simulate a nuclear underwater shock environment or nuclear air blast environment from a far field location. description: Danės upės Klaipėdos miesto savivaldybės teritorijoje valymo, gilinimo ir tvarkymo darbų projekto parengimo paslaugų pirkimo RINKOS KONSULTACIJA. Rinkos konsultacija skelbiama iki pirkimo pradžios. Rinkos konsultacija nėra skelbimas apie pirkimą ar išankstinis skelbimas apie pirkimą. Šios rinkos konsultacijos paskelbimu dalyviai nėra kviečiami varžytis dėl pirkimo sutarties. Dalyvavimas rinkos konsultacijoje yra neatlygintinas, nesuteikiantis pirmenybinio statuso dalyvaujant pirkime. Jokios išlaidos dalyviams neatlyginamos, kompensacijos nemokamos, dalyvavimas rinkos konsultacijoje neturi įtakos ir nesuteikia dalyviui pirmenybės viešiesiems pirkimams, kurie bus skelbiami ateityje, ar jų rezultatams. Rinkos konsultacijos tikslas - informuoti tiekėjus apie planuojamą pirkimą, išsiaiškinti įvairius su pirkimo objektu susijusius klausimus, pasiruošti pirkimui įvertinant pateiktus dokumentus.

title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services - Bismark, ND
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Bismark, ND area. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. You will need the adobe acrobat reader for .pdf files (www.adobe.com) in order to open most files posted by the New Orleans District. You are encouraged, for marketing purposes, to register as an Interested Vendor in beta.Sam.gov (www.beta.SAM.gov). title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services - Helena, MT
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Helena, MT area. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. Place of Performance The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Helena, MT. Interested parties must be located no more than 50 miles from the Helena, MT area. Period of Performance On or about October 1, 2026 � September 30, 2026 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. title: Air Force Civil Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
description: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services. These capabilities align with definitions in the DOD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms. AFCAP provides a full range of Base Operating/Life Support (BOS/BLS) and logistical support on an as-required basis to support a wide spectrum of activities, including, but are not limited to: Major Theater War(s); Small Scale Contingencies; Irregular Warfare; responses to Violent Extremist Organizations (VEO); foreign assistance, developmental assistance, humanitarian assistance, and security assistance (including Foreign Military Sales); peacekeeping; counterinsurgency, counterdrug and counterterrorism operations; maritime security operations; recovery operations and denial measures; domestic/international emergency support; infrastructure/facility design/build, design/build/operate, demolition, and site restoration; deliberate and crisis action planning; and military exercises (including Joint Chiefs of Staff sponsored) authorized by the National Command Authority.

title: National Coast Guard Museum- Facility Maintenance Services
description: The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) is conducting market research to identify capable sources, including small businesses (such as 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, and WOSB), to provide comprehensive 24/7 Facility Maintenance services for the newly constructed National Coast Guard Museum in New London, Connecticut. The selected contractor will be required to furnish all management, supervision, labor, equipment, and materials necessary to ensure safe, reliable, and compliant museum operations. The facility consists of an 84,000 sq. ft., six-story waterfront building situated on under 1 acre of grounds. Core requirements include, but are not limited to: HVAC & Environmental Controls: Continuous operation and maintenance of gas-fired condensing boilers, chillers, cooling towers, radiant flooring, and Building Automation Systems (BAS) to maintain strict gallery climate tolerances (68�F�72�F and 45%�55% Relative Humidity). Electrical, Plumbing, & Life Safety: Operations and maintenance of power distribution panels, emergency generators, fuel systems, fire alarms, fire extinguishers (NFPA 10), and water sprinkler systems (NFPA 25). Vertical Transportation: Monthly servicing, emergency response, and annual certified load testing for four (4) elevators. Custodial Services: A hybrid staffing model providing APPA Level 1 (Orderly Spotlessness) cleaning standards in high-traffic public galleries and APPA Level 4 in back-of-house staff areas. Grounds, Hardscape, & Snow Removal: Year-round exterior upkeep, power washing, and 24/7 bare-pavement snow and ice control (utilizing hardscape-safe compounds) for walkways, terraces, and flat roofing. Support Services: Integrated Pest Management (artifact-safe), catering kitchen equipment upkeep, and refuse/recycling stream management. Note: Museum artifacts, exhibit curation, and IT network infrastructure are excluded from this scope. See attachments for additional details

title: DLA Medical Equipment Electronic CATalog (ECAT) Generation V Program
description: Synopsis of Standing Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 DLA Troop Support, in an effort to improve medical supply support to our customers, developed the Electronic Catalog (ECAT) System. The ECAT System allows DLA Troop Support customers to review and compare contractor electronic catalogs with the ultimate goal of placing on-line orders to the contractor of their choice. Customers are currently using the ECAT System to order medical equipment and related supplies. Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 is a Request for Proposal (RFP) from which the Government will contemplate awards of contracts for Medical Equipment items as prescribed in the attached solicitation documents. This is the follow-on solicitation to our expired standing solicitation, SPE2DH-16-R-0002, which closed on August 15, 2021. This solicitation is a standing solicitation from which the Government contemplates award of contracts for medical equipment, accessories, and consumables. The solicitation will remain in effect five years from the issue date or when it is replaced by an updated solicitation, whichever comes first. Offerors are requested to submit complete proposals for all requirements, including all certifications, as specified in this solicitation. Proposals may be submitted at anytime during the open periods of the solicitation. DLA Troop Support intends to award multiple contracts to manufacturers, distributors and other specifically designated sources that support programs. The Government intends to award a contract to all responsible offerors who comply with the terms and conditions of the solicitation and whose prices are determined to be fair and reasonable. Any offeror that takes exception to any term or condition of the solicitation may be excluded from consideration for award. The items within scope of this solicitation are commercial medical equipment used by medical professionals, technicians, and laboratory personnel to perform a treatment, test, or operation, or to provide medical care for a patient. The scope of the solicitation also includes consumables and accessories for commercial medical equipment. Also included within the scope of the solicitation are medical simulation equipment used for training purposes. Please review solicitation pages 33-36 'Statement of Work' which outlines scope of products for consideration and product exclusions. The standing solicitation is also available via download from the DLA Internet Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ . Amendment 0001 issued against solicitation SPE2DH21R0002- 30 NOV 2022.

title: Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program Multi-Mission Dry Dock, Multiple Award Construction Contract
description: Title: SIOP MMDD MACCThe Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) has a requirement to provide predominantly construction services (design build (DB) and design-bid-build (DBB)) for heavy and civil engineering waterfront facilities as well as commercial and institutional facilities primarily in support of the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP) Multi-Mission Dry Dock (MMDD) at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF), located at Naval Base Kitsap (NBK) Bremerton, Washington and other areas under the cognizance of NAVFAC Pacific. This solicitation will result in the award of Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Construction Contracts (MACC). The period of performance will be a base period of 5-years and one (1) 5-year option period for a maximum possible duration of 10-years; or an aggregate maximum estimated value of $15,000,000,000 for all task orders, whichever occurs first. The typical size of major construction task orders will range from $2,000,000,000 to $6,000,000,000; however, smaller task orders may be issued to support smaller efforts such as Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) and/or Alternative Technical Concepts (ATC). Task orders may be above this limit; however, contractors are not obligated to accept such task orders under the general terms of the contract. Each MACC holder will receive a minimum guarantee in the amount of $1,000,000. This solicitation is unrestricted allowing for full and open competition. Large businesses are advised that an acceptable small business subcontracting plan is required. Primary North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction; Small Business Size Standard: $45M. Secondary NAICS code 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction; Small Business Size Standard: $45M. See attached solicitiation SF 1442 for additional details. Pre-Proposal Conference. A pre-proposal conference is scheduled for 15 October 2026, 9:00 am to 12:00 pm (PST). The pre-proposal conference will be conducted both in-person and virtually (online). Prospective Offerors are advised that the pre-proposal conference will be held solely for the purpose of explaining the concepts involved in the project and the specifications, terms and conditions of this solicitation. title: Air Force Civil Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
description: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services. These capabilities align with definitions in the DOD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms. AFCAP provides a full range of Base Operating/Life Support (BOS/BLS) and logistical support on an as-required basis to support a wide spectrum of activities, including, but are not limited to: Major Theater War(s); Small Scale Contingencies; Irregular Warfare; responses to Violent Extremist Organizations (VEO); foreign assistance, developmental assistance, humanitarian assistance, and security assistance (including Foreign Military Sales); peacekeeping; counterinsurgency, counterdrug and counterterrorism operations; maritime security operations; recovery operations and denial measures; domestic/international emergency support; infrastructure/facility design/build, design/build/operate, demolition, and site restoration; deliberate and crisis action planning; and military exercises (including Joint Chiefs of Staff sponsored) authorized by the National Command Authority.

title: Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program Multi-Mission Dry Dock, Multiple Award Construction Contract
description: Title: SIOP MMDD MACC. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) has a requirement to provide predominantly construction services (design build (DB) and design-bid-build (DBB)) for heavy and civil engineering waterfront facilities as well as commercial and institutional facilities primarily in support of the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP) Multi-Mission Dry Dock (MMDD) at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF), located at Naval Base Kitsap (NBK) Bremerton, Washington and other areas under the cognizance of NAVFAC Pacific. This solicitation will result in the award of Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Construction Contracts (MACC). The period of performance will be a base period of 5-years and one (1) 5-year option period for a maximum possible duration of 10-years; or an aggregate maximum estimated value of $15,000,000,000 for all task orders, whichever occurs first. The typical size of major construction task orders will range from $2,000,000,000 to $6,000,000,000; however, smaller task orders may be issued to support smaller efforts such as Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) and/or Alternative Technical Concepts (ATC). Task orders may be above this limit; however, contractors are not obligated to accept such task orders under the general terms of the contract. Each MACC holder will receive a minimum guarantee in the amount of $1,000,000. This solicitation is unrestricted allowing for full and open competition. Large businesses are advised that an acceptable small business subcontracting plan is required. Primary North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction; Small Business Size Standard: $45M.Secondary NAICS code 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction; Small Business Size Standard: $45M. title: DLA Medical Equipment Electronic CATalog (ECAT) Generation V Program
description: Synopsis of Standing Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 DLA Troop Support, in an effort to improve medical supply support to our customers, developed the Electronic Catalog (ECAT) System. The ECAT System allows DLA Troop Support customers to review and compare contractor electronic catalogs with the ultimate goal of placing on-line orders to the contractor of their choice. Customers are currently using the ECAT System to order medical equipment and related supplies. Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 is a Request for Proposal (RFP) from which the Government will contemplate awards of contracts for Medical Equipment items as prescribed in the attached solicitation documents. This is the follow-on solicitation to our expired standing solicitation, SPE2DH-16-R-0002, which closed on August 15, 2021. This solicitation is a standing solicitation from which the Government contemplates award of contracts for medical equipment, accessories, and consumables. The solicitation will remain in effect five years from the issue date or when it is replaced by an updated solicitation, whichever comes first. Offerors are requested to submit complete proposals for all requirements, including all certifications, as specified in this solicitation. Proposals may be submitted at anytime during the open periods of the solicitation. DLA Troop Support intends to award multiple contracts to manufacturers, distributors and other specifically designated sources that support programs. The Government intends to award a contract to all responsible offerors who comply with the terms and conditions of the solicitation and whose prices are determined to be fair and reasonable. Any offeror that takes exception to any term or condition of the solicitation may be excluded from consideration for award. The items within scope of this solicitation are commercial medical equipment used by medical professionals, technicians, and laboratory personnel to perform a treatment, test, or operation, or to provide medical care for a patient. The scope of the solicitation also includes consumables and accessories for commercial medical equipment. Also included within the scope of the solicitation are medical simulation equipment used for training purposes. Please review solicitation pages 33-36 'Statement of Work' which outlines scope of products for consideration and product exclusions. The standing solicitation is also available via download from the DLA Internet Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ . title: Helmet-Mounted First-Person View Display System
description: I. Description USSOCOM is conducting market research to identify sources capable of providing dismounted Special Operations Forces with a helmet-mounted first-person view (FPV) display. This display must deliver an expanded field of view, certified ballistic protection, real-time tactical information overlay, and unmanned system control in contested, congested, and all-weather environments. The effort aims to develop a 50-degree field-of-view Display Module that integrates full military ballistic protection, ATAK capability, head tracking, improved display performance, and expanded environmental durability while remaining compatible with existing soldier systems and helmets. This announcement is for market research purposes only and is not a solicitation. The Government will use responses to this notice to assess interest and capability within the industry and to determine the acquisition strategy (e.g., limited competition or small business set-aside). This Sources Sought is posted as a Call to Vulcan and all responses must be submitted to Vulcan. II. Requested Information Interested vendors are requested to submit the following information: Company Information: Company name, address, point of contact, CAGE code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CMMC/NIST (type, date, score), website. Business Size: Indicate your business size and socio-economic status (e.g., small business, 8(a), HUBZone, etc.). Confirm your business size relative to 541715 � Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). Security Clearance: Indicate your current facility clearance and the level of facility security clearances you can maintain. Relevant Experience: Provide a brief overview of your experience in supporting SOF, system testing, commercial integration, and ATAK areas as listed below. If no experience, briefly identify the names and CAGE codes of any small businesses that have demonstrated experience that your company can team/partner with on this requirement. Display Systems. System testing (researching, planning, designing, developing, analyzing, and testing a variety of electronic equipment and systems, military command, control, communications, computers, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (C5ISR) systems, interface units, and other electronic devices and test equipment) to support enhanced situational awareness, command and control, and precision effects while retaining mobility, protection, and compatibility with existing soldier equipment. Experience with existing soldier equipment (ATAK EUD, radios, hubs). Experience with researching, testing, and integrating emerging technologies as they pertain to real-time overlay of ATAK tactical data, targeting information, and UAS video/control in day, night, and all-weather contested environments. Capability Statement: Submit a capability statement that responds to the following questions: Describe your company�s relevant experience providing SOF support in any of the following areas: ATAK interface, ballistic protection integration, development testing, head tracking sensor integration, software updates and integration, integrating processing hardware and the Display Module into a single module, Windblast compatibility, Expanded environmental envelope, similar requirements or related mission sets. Include contract numbers, customers, and scope. Explain your approach to development milestones (SRR, PDR, CDR, development tests, prototype deliveries) for the combined work scope versus individual items and identify any related any similar efforts. Confirm your company�s ability to maintain adherence to milestones and react to shifts within technology or supply chains to avoid impact to development and enable future scaling of production. Describe your recruiting, screening, and retention strategy for specialized Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). Explain how your company would manage and execute a contract for this development. What program management tools, structures, or practices will ensure successful delivery? Describe your Quality Assurance/Quality Control processes and how they would ensure compliance with the Statement of Objectives (SOO), Key Performance Parameters (KPPs) and Key System Attributes (KSAs). If applicable, identify any suppliers, subcontractors or teaming partners. Specify their roles and the percentage of work they are expected to perform. Identify any services within the SOO that meet the definition of commercial services under FAR 2.101. Provide catalog pricing or related contract references. Provide feedback on a recommendation on contract type and structure (length, phases, single award, FFP/CPFF, OTA). Are there any risks or constraints that may affect your participation? Identify how the USSOCOM can best structure these contract requirements to facilitate competition by and among small business concerns. Identify any condition or action that may be having the effect of unnecessarily restricting competition with respect to this acquisition. Provide the specific aspects that unreasonably restrict competition and the rationale for such conclusion. Recommendations to improve the approach/specifications/NAICS/PSC/ DRAFT SOO to acquiring the identified items/services. III. Submission Details Submission Deadline: 3:00 Eastern on 01-DEC-2026 Submission Location: All submissions shall be made within https://vulcan-sof.com/ Submit To: https://vulcan-sof.com/login/ng2/submission?collectionUuid=a26a99ef-c351-464f-af93-dbcc064df521 IV. Disclaimer This Sources Sought is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal. Responses will not be returned, and the Government will not reimburse costs incurred in response preparation. Participation in this notice is not a guarantee of future contract award.

title: Preventive Maintenance and Repair Services - Kahuku Training Area (KTA)
description: The Regional Contracting Office Hawaii (RCO-HI) has a requirement for preventive maintenance, inspection, testing, unscheduled assessment/trouble-call, and repair services for HVAC; fire alarm and mass notification; emergency lighting and exit signs; and lightning protection systems at Kahuku Training Area, Oahu, Hawaii. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, transportation, supervision, and other resources necessary to perform the requirement in accordance with the solicitation and Performance Work Statement. This solicitation is issued as Request for Quotations (RFQ) No. W912CN27QA008 and is a 100 percent Total Small Business Set-Aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 561210. The Government contemplates award of one firm-fixed-price requirements contract consisting of a base period and four 12-month option periods, with evaluation of the six-month option to extend services under FAR 52.217-8. The solicitation is conducted under the provisions of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. To be eligible for award, quoters must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), including current and complete representations and certifications, at the time of quote submission and at the time of award. Quoters are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for amendments and other solicitation information through the closing date. Refer to Section L, pages 113�116, for quote-submission instructions and required submission content, and Section M, pages 120�121, for evaluation criteria. Quoters must submit all required documents, including the signed SF 1449 and acknowledgement of all amendments, completed pricing documents for all applicable priced CLINs, and the technical capability submission. Do not price Repair Services CLIN 0006 or its option-year counterparts; repair services will be ordered and priced after award through Contracting Officer-issued firm-fixed-price task orders. Written questions are due no later than 10:00 a.m. Hawaii Standard Time (HST), Thursday, 12 November 2026. title: KC-130J � In-Flight Refueling Aircraft Parts & Equipment
description: 1 PROGRAM BACKGROUND: This sources sought is issued by the Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Patuxent River, MD. The U.S. Marine Corp (USMC) and U.S. Navy Reserves (USNR) Tactical Air Lift Program (KC-130J Aircraft) PMA-207 is conducting a market survey of industry to determine potential interested sources that can provide In-Flight Refueling (IFR) aircraft pods, pods parts, fuse tank parts and equipment manufacturing; associated equipment including spares, repair parts, support equipment, technical manuals, training; and logistical engineering and field technical support. This market research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible vendors of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. Responses will also be utilized by the Government for market research purposes in developing its acquisition/contracting strategy. All interested parties must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) government website at www.sam.gov to be eligible for award of Government contracts. This sources sought is used as a market research tool pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 10 to determine potential sources and their technical capabilities. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code currently assigned to this procurement is 336413 � Aircraft Auxiliary Parts. The product service code (PSC) is 1680 - Miscellaneous Aircraft Accessories and Components. In-Flight Refueling parts/equipment is currently employed on USMC and USNR C-130 aircraft and meets System Performance Specifications for the KC-130J Tanker Aircraft, Model 382U-UUS-93, dated 23 March 2012. The Government does not have the sufficient data rights from the Original Equipment manufacturer to provide a technical data package to manufacture the required parts. All businesses that can meet the requirements of the specification are encouraged to respond. DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND MUST NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. Any resultant solicitation(s) will be released on the SAM government website. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor SAM for additional information as the direct method of communication with the Government. 2. SCOPE: The Government requires responses to this Sources Sought to be focused on the parts/equipment to be manufactured. Capable vendors must be able to manufacture and provide the parts/equipment listed below. P/N NOMENCLATURE Hose End Fitting 149C5007-1 Spring Seat 233-5011-2 Bumper Assy 149B5019 Pressure Regulator 6315-2 Drogue Tube 149D6050-4 Reception Coupling 60381-4 / 61520-4 Guillotine 149D6009-102 Ring 149B5030 Surge Suppressor 401702-1 Adapter, Coupling 149B5006 Hose Reel 149R1050-110 Ejection Spring 149-5079 Retaining Wire 149A5008 Ring Assy 227-5020 High Speed Para drogue 149D5047-3 Aerial Refueling Pumps 6300-10 Boost Pump/ Transfer Pump 60-371C Tail Cone Assembly 440080-1 Fuel Level Control Valve 4-1058-201 Capable Vendors must be able to provide the following: Potential training for installation and maintenance of the parts; Logistical support for shipping and inventory tracking; Engineering support to ensure the required parts conform to the specifications; and Field technical support to assist with troubleshooting during installation. 3. Sources Sought Respondent Instructions 3.1 The capabilities statement must include the following: The capability statement must describe the ability to obtain the technical data necessary to manufacture C-130J In-Flight Refueling parts and equipment. 3.2 Specific Sources Sought Information Requested Provide points of contact for existing or previous customers; Summary of successful operational experience in manufacturing, sustaining engineering to ensure the parts conform to the requirements; Summary of logistics support offered to include inventory tracking for shipping; Estimated timeline to obtain the required technical data, manufacture and delivery of parts; Ability to provide training for the use, repair, and maintenance of these parts/equipment; Describe engineering and/or logistical support that can be provided for the use and/or repair of these parts/equipment; Describe field technical support that can be provided for the use and/or repair of these parts/equipment; Provide company designation as a small business, large business, 8(a), etc.; and Provide the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code or Product Service Code (PSC). 4. ELIGIBILITY: The applicable NAICS code currently assigned to this procurement is 336413 � Aircraft Auxiliary Parts, and the Product Service Code (PSC) for this requirement is 1680 � Miscellaneous Aircraft Accessories and Components. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. SUBMITTAL INFORMATION (CAPABILITIES STATEMENT) Interested parties must adhere to the following instructions for the submittal of their capabilities statements. Page Limit and Format: A maximum of a two (2) 8.5 X 11 inches pages in Times New Roman font not less than 10 point. Document Type: Microsoft Word (2016) or Adobe PDF format. Delivery: Electronic submission within SAM.gov Sources Sought Notice Response date: Responses are due by 3:00 PM Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) 01 December 2026. No classified information shall be submitted in response to this Sources Sought. No telephone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the POCs listed at the end of this notice All responses must include: Sources Sought Notice name/number Company Name CAGE code Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Company Address Company Business Size: Large business or qualify as a Small Business (SB), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), HUBZone Small Business (HUBZone), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), or Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Concern. Points of Contact (POC), including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. 8. All data received in response to this Sources Sought Notice that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. Please mark all documentation with the appropriate distribution statements, if applicable. Contractors should appropriately mark any data that is proprietary or has restricted data rights. 9. Any information or materials provided in response to this Sources Sought Notice will not be returned. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this Sources Sought Notice. RESPONSES: Interested businesses must submit responses by email to the Contract Specialist, Ms. Stephanie Baker (stephanie.m.baker30.civ@us.navy.mil). The capability statement package should demonstrate the respondent�s ability to provide the requirements as listed above. CONTRACT SPECIALIST Name: Stephanie Baker Email: stephanie.m.baker30.civ@us.navy.mil CONTRACTING OFFICER Name: Shawn Campbell Email: shawn.campbell.civ@us.navy.mil In addition, please send an electronic copy of responses to: tracy.a.burrows2.civ@us.navy.mil

title: Refurbishment of Existing Tree Cooler, St. Joe Ranger District, Idaho Panhandle National Forests
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 1284LL27Q0008 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) Refurbishment of Existing Tree Cooler. Services and supplies are required for the currently installed tree cooler for the St. Joe Ranger District, Idaho Panhandle National Forests. The tree cooler was built in 1984, the outdated HVAC system shall be replaced with a new HVAC system. The contractor shall provide a fully functioning new HVAC system for the existing tree cooler with associated evaporator fans and necessary materials for the refrigeration system. Contractor shall remove any humidifiers and associated parts, update the lighting, and install a notification system of a power outage due to ongoing power fluctuations. The contractor shall provide the personnel, materials, and equipment needed to perform the required services to industry standards and specifications. Representative shall communicate with POC regarding any issues that may arise. Contractor shall coordinate work hours with CO and COR for site access, hours, and operation. There will be no Government Property issued. Electricity will be available on site for Contractor's use. All work shall be completed by 03/15/2027. See attachment 1284LL27Q0008 for more details. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 811310 The small business size standard is $12.5 million dollars. This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency.

title: CAPACITY ON A UHF-CAPABLE ON-ORBIT MEO SATELLITE
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is focused on obtaining access to bandwidth carried by a commercially owned, commercially operated UHF-capable on-orbit MEO satellite for use in a near-term experimental campaign to: Characterize spectrum, waveform, and user equipment operation with a MEO UHF system Demonstrate interoperability between a potential future MEO UHF system and the existing GEO constellation Inform a time-sequenced pathway to augment or replace the GEO UHF system with a MEO capability The offeror should consider technology solutions that prioritize existing space vehicle, payload and communications link capabilities to provide on-orbit service immediately or as soon as possible. An Initial Launch Capability (ILC) by 2030 is potentially useful, but innovative approaches leading to earlier on-orbit capability are strongly desired. The Government recognizes that this initial prototype may not be fully representative of a final, future architecture, but rather represents an initial step to explore providing UHF services from MEO. AMENDMENT 1 (23 Jul 2026) The following changes are hereby made to the above announcement: Corrects the uplink and downlink frequency bands in Section 4.0.a.i The attachment entitled "pMEO Demo Request for Information_FINAL 10 Jul 26" is removed in its entirety and replaced with "pMEO Demo Request for Information_AMEND1 23 Jul 26". All other RFI content and due dates remain unchanged. Refer to the attachment entitled "pMEO Demo Request for Information_AMEND1 23 Jul 26" for full details.

title: CAPACITY ON A UHF-CAPABLE ON-ORBIT MEO SATELLITE
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is focused on obtaining access to bandwidth carried by a commercially owned, commercially operated UHF-capable on-orbit MEO satellite for use in a near-term experimental campaign to: Characterize spectrum, waveform, and user equipment operation with a MEO UHF system Demonstrate interoperability between a potential future MEO UHF system and the existing GEO constellation Inform a time-sequenced pathway to augment or replace the GEO UHF system with a MEO capability The offeror should consider technology solutions that prioritize existing space vehicle, payload and communications link capabilities to provide on-orbit service immediately or as soon as possible. An Initial Launch Capability (ILC) by 2030 is potentially useful, but innovative approaches leading to earlier on-orbit capability are strongly desired. title: Request For Proposal (RFP) for NASA Agency-wide Supply of Liquid and Gaseous Helium
description: Update 11/13/2026 The purpose of this announcement is to publish Amendment 0003 to Solicitation 80KSC024R0010 for the 2027 IDIQ CLIN Opt-In (Amendment 0001 and Amendment 0002 were posted with the origninal solicitation), extend the proposal due date from November 20, 2026, to December 1, 2026, and provide Questions and Answers. See attached 80KSC024R0010 Amendment 0003 IDIQ CLIN Opt-In and 80KSC024R0010 2027 IDIQ CLIN Opt-In Questions and Answers. ____________________________________________________________________ UPDATE 10/20/2026 The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) John F. Kennedy Space Center is pleased to release the 2027 NASA Agency-wide Supply of Liquid and Gaseous Helium opt-in opportunity as described in the original Helium Request for Proposal (RFP), Sections 2.10, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in, and 2.10.1, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The Helium RFP was issued on December 21, 2024, and the original solicitation (as revised) remains open throughout the ordering period through the use of innovative provisions as prescribed in Section 2.10.1, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The Helium contract's ordering period remains valid through September 30, 2030. The RFP has resulted in the award of four fixed-price indefinite delivery (ID) requirements contracts to supply liquid and gaseous helium in support of operations at agency centers and facilities across the United States. Awards were made to the following companies: Airgas USA LLC (South), Airgas USA LLC (West), Linde, Inc., and Messer LLC. Each year during the life of the solicitation and at the time established via synopsis, the Government will accept proposals from new entrants for each IDIQ subCLIN location and the Government will also accept proposals from existing helium contractors for each additional IDIQ subCLIN location. A new entrant is a company that does not currently hold a NASA liquid and gaseous helium contract. The Government will evaluate the proposals to determine technical acceptability for a specific NASA location. Upon the Government's determination of technical acceptability, a contract (for new entrants) or contract modification (for existing helium Contractors) will be executed to add the Contractor to the IDIQ CLIN Pool for the specific NASA location. Thereafter, the Contractor will be eligible to participate in the IDIQ CLIN Pool process described in Section 2.10 for the NASA locations awarded to that Contractor. All eligible Contractors who are awarded an IDIQ subCLIN for a particular NASA location will have the option to compete for requirements within those IDIQ subCLINs which they are awarded. The commodities will support current and future aerospace flight, simulation, research, development, testing, and other operations at the following NASA centers and facilities: Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility (CSBF) locations (Palestine, TX, Ft Sumner, NM, Port Hueneme, CA, and Burns, OR); Glenn Research Center (GRC), Cleveland, OH 44135; GRC Neil A. Armstrong Test Facility (GRC-ATF), Sandusky, OH 44870; Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), Greenbelt, MD 20771; Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), Pasadena, CA 91109; Johnson Space Center (JSC), Houston, TX 77058; Kennedy Space Center (KSC - including Cape Canaveral Space Force Station - CCSFS); Langley Research Center (LaRC), Hampton, VA 23666; Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC), Huntsville, AL, 35812; Michoud Assembly Facility (MAF), New Orleans, LA 70129; Stennis Space Center (SSC), Stennis Space Center, MS, 39529; White Sands Test Facility (WSTF), Las Cruces, NM 88012; and other such places of performance as required in this contract. Submission information: 1. Opt-in by a Current Helium Contractor. A current Helium Contractor shall submit Attachment 2.1 Capability Form for each proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. The Government will evaluate the capability form to determine technical acceptability in accordance with the weekly maximums for a subCLIN location in contract Section 2.1.1 Schedule of Supplies Table for Gaseous and Liquid Helium - Requirements. If the Contractor is determined technically acceptable, award will be made for the subCLIN(s). 2. Opt-in by New Entrant. The new entrant shall submit an Attachment 2.1 Capability Form for each proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. The Government will evaluate the capability form to determine technical acceptability in accordance with the weekly maximums for a subCLIN location in contract Section 2.1.1 Schedule of Supplies Table for Gaseous and Liquid Helium - Requirements. Once determined acceptable from a technical standpoint, award will be made for the subCLIN(s). New entrants will be required to comply with provisions in Section 5 of the RFP and all terms and conditions of the resulting contract. 3. All questions regarding this opt-in notice shall be submitted in writing via email to Hillary Heard at hillary.p.heard@nasa.gov, and Shana Thompson at shana.d.thompson@nasa.gov. The Government will not answer oral questions due to the possibility of misunderstanding or misinterpretation. The Offeror shall submit all questions, if any, no later than November 4, 2026, to allow for analysis and dissemination of responses in advance of the proposal due date. The Government will not guarantee a response to late questions. Questions shall not be directed to the technical activity personnel. 4. It is requested that any interested party notify the helium Contracting Officers via email no later than November 4, 2026, of your intent to submit a proposal during this opt-in period as well as the name(s) of which NASA Center(s) you intend to propose. Please send your notice of intent to propose to Hillary Heard at hillary.p.heard@nasa.gov, and Shana Thompson at shana.d.thompson@nasa.gov. 5. All offers shall be sent to Hillary Heard at hillary.p.heard@nasa.gov, and Shana Thompson at shana.d.thompson@nasa.gov by November 20, 2026, by 4:30PM EST. Late submissions will be handled in accordance with FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, paragraph (f). 6. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition is Marcus Orr, Acting Deputy Procurement Officer at marcus.c.orr@nasa.gov. ************************************** Amendment 0002. buyer: Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie GmbH (HZB)
title: Germany – Laboratory furniture – V456_2026 - HiPOLE - Laborausstattung inkl. Planung (Lab2Fab)
description: Als eines von 18 Zentren der Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft beschäftigt das Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie (HZB) rund 1.400 Mitarbeiter an den Standorten Berlin-Wannsee und Berlin-Adlershof – und verfügt über einen Gesamthaushalt von zirka 110 Millionen Euro. Das HZB arbeitet eng mit den Universitäten und Fachhochschulen in Berlin-Brandenburg zusammen. Das HZB forscht an Lösungen für eine klimaneutrale Gesellschaft. Forschende entwickeln und optimieren effiziente und preiswerte Materialien für Solarzellen, Batterien und Katalysatoren. Diese Energiematerialien sind wesentliche Bausteine auf dem Weg in eine CO2-neutrale und sichere Energieversorgung. Wichtigstes Werkzeug ist die Röntgenquelle BESSY II, welche intensives Licht im weichen Röntgenbereich liefert. Damit wird der Aufbau von Energie- und Quantenmaterialien sowie ihre Funktionsweise untersucht. Das HZB forscht auch an neuen Konzepten für beschleunigerbasierte Röntgenquellen und entwickelt neue Instrumente mit immer höheren Messgenauigkeiten. Das HZB und die Friedrich-Schiller-Universität Jena gründeten 2023 das Helmholtz-Institut für Polymere in Energieanwendungen (HIPOLE) in Jena als dauerhafte Einrichtung des HZB. Führende Expertisen in den Bereichen Energiespeicherung und Photovoltaik, polymere Materialien, künstliche Intelligenz sowie nachhaltige Chemie konnten somit gebündelt werden, um die beschleunigte wissensbasierte Erforschung nachhaltiger Polymermaterialien für skalierbare Energietechnologien voranzubringen. HIPOLE Jena basiert auf drei Forschungssäulen: • Materialdesign und Synthese • Skalierbarkeit, Prototypen und Transfer sowie • Charakterisierung, Theorie, Modellierung und Datenwissenschaften. Der Fokus liegt nicht nur in der Grundlagenforschung, sondern auch im Transfer der Forschungsergebnisse. Aktuell sind an HIPOLE Jena rund 50 Mitarbeitende beschäftigt. Die Forschungsarbeiten der Wissenschaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftler am HIPOLE Jena, unterstützt von sieben assoziierten Mitgliedern der FSU Jena und des HZB, lassen sich fünf Forschungsbereichen zuordnen: 1. Polymere Redox-Flow Batterien, 2. Polymer-basierte Dünnschichtbatterien, 3. Photovoltaik, 4. Funktionale selbstheilende Materialien und 5. Nachhaltige Chemie. Das Helmholtz-Institut für Polymere in Energieanwendungen Jena (HIPOLE Jena) beabsichtigt die Beschaffung von Laborausstattung inkl. Planung (Lab2Fab). Es sollen drei Laborräume mit Labormöbeln in bezugsfertigen Laborflächen im Lab2Fab in Jena ausgestattet werden.

description: Rajavartiolaitos (myöhemmin myös Hankintayksikkö) kilpailuttaa Ratas-järjestelmän ylläpito- ja kehittämispalvelut. Ratas-järjestelmä on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 1 "ylläpidettävän kohteen kuvaus". Ratas on käytössä oleva tietojärjestelmäkokonaisuus, jonka toiminnan jatkuvuus, käytettävyys, tietoturvallisuus ja hallittu kehittäminen ovat keskeisiä hankintayksikön toiminnan kannalta. Järjestelmää on kehitetty vaiheittain nykyisen toimintamallin mukaisesti. Tulevan kilpailutuksen tavoitteena on muodostaa pitkäjänteinen palvelumalli, jolla varmistetaan järjestelmän laadukas ylläpito sekä mahdollistetaan tarpeelliset muutokset ja jatkokehitys hallitusti. Hankinnan ensisijaisena tavoitteena on varmistaa: • järjestelmän jatkuva käytettävyys ja toimintavarmuus • tehokas häiriönhallinta ja ongelmanratkaisu • järjestelmän teknisen ympäristön ylläpito • tietoturvallinen ja hallittu muutosten toteuttaminen • tarvittavan dokumentaation ja osaamisen säilyminen • tilaajan tukeminen järjestelmän elinkaaren hallinnassa. Palvelu sisältää alustavasti seuraavia kokonaisuuksia: Ylläpitopalvelut • järjestelmän jatkuva ylläpito • häiriöiden vastaanotto, analysointi ja ratkaisu • palvelupyyntöjen käsittely • ongelmanhallinta • versio- ja muutostenhallinta • käyttöympäristön tekninen ylläpito • yhteistyö infrastruktuuri- ja muiden toimittajien kanssa. Sovellustuki ja tekninen hallinta • sovelluksen teknisen toiminnan varmistaminen • sovelluskomponenttien hallinta • tekninen selvitys- ja asiantuntijatuki • suorituskyvyn ja kapasiteetin seuranta • tietoturvallisuuden ylläpito. Jatkokehitys ja muutokset • pienimuotoiset kehitystoimenpiteet • korjaavat ja ennakoivat muutokset • toiminnalliset kehitystarpeet • tekninen velanhallinta. Varsinainen kehitystyö ei ole hankinnan pääasiallinen tavoite, vaan sen tarkoituksena on tukea järjestelmän elinkaaren hallintaa ja ylläpitopalvelun onnistumista. Jatkokehityksen osuus palvelussa on ylläpitoa täydentävä osa-alue. Sen tavoitteena on mahdollistaa tarvittavat muutokset, korjaukset ja rajatut kehitystarpeet ilman erillisiä raskaita järjestelyjä. Ratas-järjestelmää on tarkoitus jatkokehittää tulevien vuosien aikana integraatiolla European Travel Information and Authorisation System (ETIAS) -järjestelmään ja uusimalla Ratas-järjestelmän käyttäjätunnistus nykyaikaisella ratkaisulla. Osallistumispyynnön tavoitteena on tunnistaa markkinoilta rajattu määrä ehdokkaita, joilla on riittävä osaaminen ja kapasiteetti vastata Ratas-järjestelmän ylläpito- ja kehittämispalvelusta. Ratas-järjestelmä tullaan korvaamaan nykyisen suunnitelman mukaan ensi vuosikymmenen puolella. Korvaavan järjestelmän hankinnan yksityiskohdat ovat vielä päättämättä.

title: Rosebud Lift Station Construction
description: The existing lift station has been in place since the early 1990s. Since its creation the hospital anticipates increased expansion in the emergency department, added on Tribal programs (dialysis, detox, Tribal Health Administration Building), added on 19 more quarters units, and is anticipating adding an additional 23 quarters units. The existing pumps are facing replacement every 1-2 years due to the unanticipated growth, but due to the growth we need to consider increasing the capacity of the wet well. In addition to switching from standard submersible pumps to chopper pumps to accommodate the random objects that get flushed into the system. In July both pumps ended up failing and they had to not only replace the pumps but pay for sewage disposal to circumvent overflow. A separate project is in the works to begin remediating/replacing damaged sewer mains due to inflow and infiltration. This construction solicitation will require the full removal and replacement of the lift station for the Rosebud complex. The existing lift station provides wastewater service to the hospital quarters units, and several tribal program buildings. Once installation is complete the new lift station will take the full sanitary load for the area currently being serviced by the existing lift station and be sized to handle expansion in the future. Then the existing lift station consisting of the wet well, dry well, pumps and piping will be demolished. The new lift station will consist of a wet well, a dry well, installation of chopper pumps, and force main connection. This project will also include a new control system to allow the facility to monitor flow into the lift station and the status of the equipment. Brand Names: Where brand names are referenced, they establish a standard of quality and performance. Offerors may propose equal products that meet or exceed the specified functional and performance requirements. The Government will evaluate equality based on technical compatibility, performance, and integration with the system.

title: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) PEO-SDA
description: SAM.GOV Special Notice Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) H9241525X0001 US Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) PEO SOF Digital Applications (SDA) SECTION 1 � INTRODUCTION 1.1 USSOCOM Special Operations Forces Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics (SOF AT&L) seeks to accelerate the application of commercially derived software innovation into deployable warfighting capabilities in support of Special Operations Forces (SOF). Early identification of warfighter needs and continuous engagement with users during software development and fielding will support increased lethality and efficiency. 1.2 In order to support rapid fielding of tailored software capabilities, SOF AT&L seeks to award FAR and non-FAR contracts and agreements to non-traditional and traditional defense contractors to carry out prototype projects for Program Executive Office SOF Digital Applications (PEO SDA) that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of software intensive programs, platforms, components, algorithms, and processes. As such, under the authority of 10 USC � 3458 and DoD Class Deviation 2022-O0007, USSOCOM SOF AT&L releases this Commercial Solutions Opening. This CSO may result in an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) or a FAR-based contract. 1.3 This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) will make awards to proposals for innovative, commercial technologies through multi-phased, competitive processes throughout 2024 and 2025. Awards may include prototypes as well as concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile software development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for defense application. Interested vendors should note that all of PEO SDA�s Programs of Record are being managed in accordance with DoDI 5000.87, the software acquisition pathway, for the timely acquisition of custom software capabilities developed for the DoD. Programs will require government and contractor software teams to use modern iterative software development methodologies (e.g., agile or lean), modern tools and techniques (e.g., development, security, and operations (DevSecOps)), and human-centered design processes to iteratively deliver software to meet the users� priority needs. 1.3.1 Phase I: Solutions will be sought on a full-and-open basis under certain Technology Areas of Interest (AOI) relevant to SDA requirements. Initial submissions against 2024 and 2025 AOIs will be requested as Solution Briefs (SB). A team of Government personnel who are subject matter experts for the given AOI will evaluate each submission independently against standard criteria for advancement to Phase II. The Government may elect to proceed directly to Phase III after a successful Phase I evaluation. 1.3.2 Phase II: If a Phase II evaluation is necessary, the Government will host Phase II invitees so that each company has a standard amount of time to pitch / demonstrate its proposed solution to the Government evaluation panel and hold any discussions necessary for evaluation. Discussions may continue outside of the pitch / demonstration session. Participation in Phase II will be entirely at the company�s expense. Favorably evaluated pitches will receive a Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) that marks the beginning of Phase III. Note, Phase II is optional for the CSO process, and may not always be conducted, or may not be required for every successful Phase I submission. 1.3.3 Phase III: The Government will only advance companies to Phase III if it intends to award a contract or agreement for the proposed solution. Companies will collaboratively build Statements of Work with the Government team and negotiate Contract/Agreement Terms and Conditions for award. 1.4 Technology Areas of Interest (AOI): Specific AOIs will be posted and advertised intermittently when the Government has particular interest in a further defined problem set for software-intensive capabilities. Technology AOIs will only be posted for a specified amount of time wherein submissions will be accepted. Additionally, specific AOIs will usually have funding set-aside and available to immediately make awards for favorably evaluated proposals determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Examples of future AOIs are as follows but not limited to: The development of Software Lifecycle Management tools, Software Process Improvement/Education, Automation Tooling for Data Ingestion/Tagging, and innovating novel approaches to Machine Learning (ML) Ops processing. 1.5 This notice fulfills synopsis requirements. Synopsis under FAR subpart 5.2 of the individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO is not required. All Technology AOIs will be publicized at https://www.sofwerx.org. Announcements of individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO made at the SOFWERX website are considered to satisfy reasonable efforts to obtain competition in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4021 and 4022 (b)(2). SECTION 2 � GUIDELINES FOR SOLUTION BRIEFS, PITCHES, AND PROPOSALS 2.1 The purpose of the Solution Brief is to identify innovative solutions and preclude effort on the part of the Company whose proposed work may not be of interest to the Government. Companies are encouraged to follow the instructions detailed below. The Government aims to provide an evaluation response NLT the specified evaluation completion date after the submission against specific AOIs. 2.2 Submissions will not be returned. The original of each submission received will be retained by USSOCOM and all other non-required copies destroyed. 2.3 Guidelines for Solution Brief Submissions: 2.3.1 It is generally desired that active Research and Development (R&D) and technology application is underway for potential solutions submitted under this CSO. Active R&D includes analytical studies and laboratory studies to physically validate the analytical predictions of separate elements of the technology, as well as software engineering and development. Technology application in this case refers to a variety of methods to validate dissimilar capabilities that may be modified to meet a need. 2.3.2 Costs of preparing and submitting solution briefs are at the Company�s expense. 2.3.3 Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. 2.3.4 An overview diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. 2.3.5 Multiple solution briefs addressing different technology AOIs may be submitted by the same organization; however, each solution brief may only address one solution based on the specific AOI. 2.3.6 The period of performance for any solution brief or proposal submitted under this CSO should generally be no greater than 24 months. 2.3.7 Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation. 2.3.8 All solution briefs shall be unclassified. Solution briefs containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences on the cover page: �This solution brief includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government, except to contractor support services personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this Company as a result of - or in connection with - the submission of this data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the Government's right to use information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets] and each restricted data sheet should be marked as follows: �
